_comment: The map DELTA builds for itself: Depth Anything depth, scaled to metres
by stereo, carved into a grid of vertical columns.
Ported from the glasses project's map.json. The scale settings are
unchanged -- they are about the depth model, not the robot. The grid is
new, because the glasses stored one height per square and the drone
stores a whole column. See delta/gap_map.py for why.
_every_n_frames: Depth Anything is the slow stage. Mapping on every other frame keeps the drone responsive to the keys.

_comment: Stereo is the ruler. The surface fit uses pixels where both stereo and
Depth Anything have a value, 0.3-6 m. Measured in the glasses project:
a narrower 0.5-3 m band failed on views close to a wall.
cell x cell metres per floor square, stacked `height_m / layer` layers
high. 0.10 m layers because the drone is 0.30 m across: three layers
per drone is enough to tell a gap it fits through from one it does not,
without making the array four times bigger than it needs to be.
height_m is 3.0: one storey. This map does not stack floors -- heights
are measured from the floor beneath the drone, so an upstairs would be
written over the downstairs. V1 maps the storey the drone is on.
grid._max_range: Beyond 4 m the depth error is larger than a grid square, so a further reading writes the wrong square confidently.
grid._stride: Every 3rd pixel for surfaces. The picture has far more pixels than the grid has squares.
_carve: Marking empty space costs carve_samples writes per pixel, so it runs on
a coarser stride than the surface pass. carve_margin is how far short of
the surface to stop -- a little more than one grid square, so a ray
never carves away the very wall it just measured.
_hits: Votes are per FRAME, not per pixel: a layer seen in two separate frames,
from two viewpoints. The glasses project counted pixels, which let one
frame's speckle clear the threshold by itself.
